eHealth & the Internet

eHealth — telehealth, mobile health, patient portals and reliable online health information.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define eHealth and telehealth
  • Describe mobile health and patient portals
  • Explain how to evaluate online health information

In simple words

eHealth uses the internet and digital technologies for health care and health information. Telehealth is care delivered at a distance using technology.

Nurses should guide patients to reliable online health information and understand telehealth basics.

eHealth tools

Tool Example
Telehealth Video consultation with a doctor
mHealth Health apps on a phone
Patient portal Online access to records and messages
eLearning Online nursing education
Social media Health education and support groups

Evaluating online health information

  • Who runs the site? (government, university, hospital — more trustworthy)
  • Is the information current? (check the date)
  • Is it evidence-based? (references to research)
  • Is it trying to sell something? (be cautious)

Nurse’s role

  • Teach patients to use patient portals.
  • Support telehealth visits (help with technology).
  • Guide patients to reliable websites.
  • Warn against unreliable or commercial health claims.
  • Protect privacy during telehealth visits.

🔴 eHealth supports care

eHealth uses digital technology for health care and information — telehealth, apps and patient portals support, but do not replace, in-person care.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Telehealth visits — help patients connect; ensure privacy; assist with the technology.
  • Patient portal — show patients how to view results and message the team.
  • Health education — recommend reliable websites; warn against commercial claims.
  • mHealth apps — suggest reputable apps for medication reminders or tracking.
  • Continuing education — use eLearning for your own learning.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. eHealth uses the internet and digital technology for health care and information.
  2. Tools: telehealth, mHealth, patient portals, eLearning.
  3. Telehealth delivers care at a distance using technology.
  4. Evaluate websites: who runs it, is it current, is it evidence-based.
  5. eHealth supports — does not replace — in-person care.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Patient portals give online access to records and messaging.
  2. mHealth apps can remind about medications or track health.
  3. Protect privacy during telehealth visits.
  4. Guide patients to government, university or hospital websites.

📌 Memory trick

Website credibility: “C-E-E” — Current, Evidence-based, Expert source.

60-second revision

  • eHealth = digital technology for health care and information.
  • Tools: telehealth, mHealth, patient portals, eLearning.
  • Telehealth = care at a distance.
  • Check websites: current, evidence-based, expert source.
  • eHealth supports in-person care.

Test yourself

eHealth uses:

Answer: B. eHealth uses the internet and digital technologies for health care and information.

Telehealth is:

Answer: B. Telehealth delivers care at a distance using technology such as video.

When evaluating a health website, check:

Answer: B. Check who runs the site, whether it is current and evidence-based.

A patient portal allows patients to:

Answer: B. Patient portals give online access to records and secure messaging.

eHealth:

Answer: B. eHealth supports — does not replace — in-person care.
